A1.justification: Both complete, readable 30-page PDFs describe the same work. Text, equations, figures, references, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison; pages 11–30 are identical in both extracted text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original simulations of heterogeneous logistic regression and AC optimal power flow on IEEE-39 and IEEE-118 bus systems in Section 6 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains these original logistic-regression and optimal-power-flow simulations, including the convergence results in Figures 2–3.

M1.justification: Sections 2–5 retain the same equality- and inequality-constrained FL formulations, FL-proximal and FL-Newton variants, and discrete- and continuous-time momentum procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic heterogeneous logistic-regression task and AC optimal power flow on IEEE-39 and IEEE-118 bus systems. No dataset, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Figures 2–3 retain the same comparisons among FL-proximal, FL-momentum, and FL-Newton in each experiment. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 6 retains the same data generation, five logistic-regression clients with 200 samples each, and evaluation procedures. The objective-value and KKT-gap plots retain their metrics and iteration ranges.

E4.justification: The simulation comparisons are unchanged, and neither version adds or removes ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness tests, error analyses, or supplementary empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figures 2–3 retain the same convergence curves without uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: The plotted results and accompanying passages in Section 6 are identical. Both retain momentum's faster convergence than FL-proximal on IEEE-39 and their nearly overlapping curves on IEEE-118; no result entries or values change.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Assumptions 1–4, Theorems 1–5, and proofs and auxiliary derivations in Appendices B–F are unchanged. Different page breaks do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: global KKT convergence, the connection to SQP, extension to inequality constraints, and momentum acceleration with continuous-time convergence guarantees.

C2.justification: Both retain the same qualifications about restrictive assumptions, unresolved discrete-time and inequality-momentum convergence, and Theorem 5 establishing convergence without proving acceleration. The IEEE-118 ill-conditioning hypothesis also remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 6 provides identical experimental and data-generation details. No implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware information, or code/data access information are added, removed, or revised.

R1.justification: The references and related-work discussion in Appendix A are identical. The positioning relative to earlier feedback-linearization, SQP, and acceleration research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Page 1 updates Zhang's affiliation from Harvard to MIT, changes the surname spelling Raghunathan to Raghunanthan, revises contact and date information, and adds NSF funding acknowledgments. Scientific prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Affiliations move from the title block into expanded footnotes, shifting the abstract and reflowing pages 1–10, including Figure 1's position. All figure images remain identical, and pages 11–30 retain the same layout.

improvement.justification: The revision updates author information and funding disclosure and modestly reformats the front matter. The scientific exposition, methods, theory, experimental evidence, limitations, and appendices remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
